attribution.source: this project — read from the handlers themselves
attribution.method: Each handler was disassembled inside its own extent and read for what it does to the context, to the object it points at, or to the globals it calls. Names are descriptive, not the original developers' names; they say what the code does, not what it was called.
attribution.distinct_from: fixtures/scd/opcodes.json — that file is transcribed from the MIT-licensed OpenBiohazard2 and its names DO come from the original developers' symbols. Where both exist, the licensed name always wins and this file is ignored.
attribution.marker: tools/walk_stream.py prints an inferred name with a leading '~' so the two can never be confused.

0x00.name: Nop
0x00.evidence: 0x8006db14: advance 1, return 1 - the one-byte NOP. Decoded predecessors are 0x02 (7202) and itself (3993), and its runs are short, so it pads between commands rather than marking empty space.

0x02.name: CondEnd
0x02.evidence: 0x8006db84: advance 1, return 2 (not 1 like the 0x00 NOP). Follows Compare 6261 times in the corpus, i.e. it terminates a condition.

0x05.name: ClearSlot
0x05.evidence: 0x8006dbf4: reads byte 1 as an index, computes a 0x6c-strided offset into the table at 0x80113ad0, clears byte 1 of that entry, advances 2 - a per-slot deactivate.

0x08.name: EndBlock
0x08.evidence: 0x8006dcac: pops the frame (ctx+0x140 -= 4), advances 2, decrements the thread's block depth. The counterpart of 0x07, which pops the same frame and jumps.

0x0a.name: WaitCount
0x0a.evidence: 0x8006dd28: decrements a u16 counter at 160(thread) and does NOT advance while it is non-zero, so the dispatcher re-runs the same command. Advance 3 only on expiry.

0x0e.name: LoopWhile
0x0e.evidence: 0x8006df78: same counter, but while it is non-zero it reloads ctx+0x1c from a saved slot at 32(thread) — a loop back to a recorded target; on expiry it advances 2 and drops the block depth.

0x20.name: Fill
0x20.evidence: Shares the same NOP handler at 0x8006db14, so its *semantics* are identical; the data distinguishes it. 7147 of 7753 occurrences are followed by another 0x20, in 606 runs with median 10, p90 31 and max 62 (191 runs are >= 20 long, covering 5254 occurrences). So 0x20 marks long empty stretches, where 0x00 pads between commands. Which one an interpreter sees is decidable only by reachability, not by behaviour - see M149.

0x28.name: Rand
0x28.evidence: 0x8006eae0: advances 1 and calls FUN_8006d284, a generator - seed = seed + ((seed & 0x7fffffff) >> 15) + (seed & 0x7fff8000)*2, storing the low halfword in DAT_800e8cb2. Followed by itself 1018 times, i.e. several rolls in a row.

0x2f.name: SetMotion
0x2f.evidence: 0x8006fd30: reads byte 1 as a slot index and a u16 at byte 2, writes it to 344(ctx + slot*8) — the very halfword 0x30 reads back.

0x30.name: ApplyMotion
0x30.evidence: 0x8006fd58: adds ctx+344/346/348 to the object's position fields 40/44/48 and ctx+350/352/354 to its angles 100/102/104, then advances 1. The consumer for 0x2f.

0x81.name: StateDispatch
0x81.evidence: 0x800727b0: tests a global flag byte (& 0x80), loads a table byte at 6169, then dispatches on the command's two operand bytes through a table at 0x800c…

0x82.name: ReleaseByKey
0x82.evidence: 0x800716b0: calls FUN_800717a0(byte1, byte2), then walks a table of 124-byte entries clearing those whose field 108 matches the result (zeroes bytes 0, 1 and halfword 24). Byte 1 == 6 takes a separate path to FUN_80038ff0.

0x84.name: SndMode
0x84.evidence: 0x80073448: writes a mode byte (4), sets a flag byte to 1, ORs 0x8000 into a state word at 6748 and stores the command's byte 1 into a status byte; advance 2.

0x85.name: SndPlay3D
0x85.evidence: 0x800734b0: reads byte 1 (an index) and byte 2, gathers two 3-axis vectors from objects' fields 40/44/48, and calls FUN_8006ab40 with both vectors plus u16@4 and u8@3 — two positions, so a 3D source play.

0x86.name: SndBusy
0x86.evidence: 0x80073564: advances 1 and returns sltu(0, u16 at 7476) i.e. 1 while the sound state is non-zero — a predicate the dispatcher can branch on.

0x87.name: SndStop
0x87.evidence: 0x80073590: advances 1 and writes 0x01000000 to 4404(0x800e…) — a stop/pause flag.

0x88.name: CountdownSlot
0x88.evidence: 0x800728ec: advances 3, calls FUN_8008c51c(byte1); for a non-negative result it indexes 0x800c76b0 + idx*8 + 0x20000, subtracts byte 2 from the counter at 6169, and when that reaches zero clears 6168/6169/6170 and calls FUN_8008c568.
